Thought for 2m 10s

The two-call change can miss this clipping. Dropping preventScroll is not enough for the geometry you measured, and a focus-only check will still pass.

At cad85, hosted/app/phone/PhoneApp.tsx is SHA256 57543cdbc0fbcb7a51cab725d65907e76af2a29ecf9f2022bffe6caaadc9da02. The only preventScroll: true calls are the opener focus at line 426 and the editor fallback at line 429. The discard-alert effect at line 241 does not trust focus() to scroll: it follows it with scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest" }).

Cancel’s top is 832.15, inside the 844 viewport, while the dialog clips at 828. About 12px of the button already intersects the visual viewport and the rest is clipped by the dialog (scrollTop 0, scrollHeight 976, clientHeight 811). Native focus scrolling can treat that as already visible and leave scrollTop at 0. activeElement is still Cancel, so the current failure survives. Call 429 does not run once call 426 sticks, so changing the fallback cannot save this case.

Acceptance that is still missing, on this same viewport, after Keep editing:

Cancel’s full border box lies inside the dialog’s client rect, not merely inside the viewport, and dialog.scrollTop moves from 0.
The document and .phone-main scroll offsets stay unchanged.
The dirty Delete button, which sits lower than Cancel, is fully inside that same rect.
A short add form whose opener is already fully visible does not change dialog.scrollTop.
The same clipping check in Arabic. That browser pass is not done.

cad85 remains a source checkpoint. The pinned 321 + 6 result does not cover this.","heavy":"Grok
Thought for 17s

Bounded critique — Keep editing focus visibility (cad85c4)
Heavy session. Access date: 18 November 2026. Read-only. No implementation. Root owns the fix and pinned retests.

Reproduced issue (source-confirmed by root measurements)

On pushed cad85c4, Keep editing returns DOM focus into the open modal, but the Cancel button is entirely below the dialog viewport (target top 832.15 / bottom 881.15; modal clip top 16 / bottom 828; scrollTop 0; scrollHeight 976 / clientHeight 811; viewport 844). Two Keep-only native focus calls currently pass preventScroll: true.

Primary guidance
HTML Standard / MDN: HTMLElement.focus() scrolls the element into view by default. preventScroll: true suppresses that behavior. Default is preventScroll: false.
WAI-ARIA APG Dialog (Modal): keyboard focus must remain inside the dialog and, for large content, both the start of content and the focused element should remain visible. “The keyboard focus always remains visible.”
WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) and 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA, WCAG 2.2) require that a focused component is not entirely hidden.
Critique of the proposed remedy

Allowing normal native focus scrolling (removing preventScroll: true from the two Keep-only calls) matches the default HTML focus contract and the APG requirement that focused elements remain visible. The listed guards (captured-form, open-dialog, reopened-prompt, effective-disabled, hidden, no-late-focus-steal) and unchanged draft/storage are appropriate and do not conflict with the scroll change.

Distinctions
DOM focus ≠ visible focus. Root has already shown DOM focus succeeds while the target is fully outside the modal clip. The remedy addresses the visibility gap for these two calls.
Browser focus/scroll ≠ physical assistive technology. Synthetic browser measurements do not prove VoiceOver or TalkBack will scroll or announce the same way. Physical AT remains a separate gate.
Reproduced issue vs hypothesis. The measurements establish a reproduced visibility defect on cad85c4. Any residual risk after the change (partial occlusion, sticky dialog header, or RTL layout shift) is a hypothesis until retested.
Concrete remaining acceptance cases (EN/AR narrow record/add forms)
Keep editing on a form whose action buttons start below the fold (current measurements). Expect: after focus, Cancel is at least partially inside the modal clip; scrollTop > 0.
Same path with Arabic labels and RTL on a 390×844 viewport. Expect: no overflow; focused Cancel remains visible.
Keep editing after a field change that re-renders the form. Expect: focus lands on Cancel (or the intended control) and that control is visible; no late focus steal.
Open dialog → Keep editing → immediate Tab/Shift-Tab. Expect: focus stays inside the dialog and the newly focused control is visible.

Current 321 main + 6 PDF / type / lint / build passes do not cover this newly reproduced visibility defect. No duplicate patch from this lane.

Critique finished. Available for the next concrete follow-up. Heavy session remains Heavy.","composer":1}
